title: General Knowledge
blurb: Geography, history, food, sport and more: a bit of everything.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Iron-rich dust on its surface gives Mars its rusty red colour.

questions.q: How many continents are there?
questions.fact: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia (Oceania), Europe, North America and South America.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific covers about a third of the whole planet.

questions.q: In which country is the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.fact: It was built about 4,500 years ago for the pharaoh Khufu.

questions.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.fact: More than 900 million people speak Mandarin as their first language.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.fact: Diamonds are made of carbon squeezed under enormous pressure deep underground.

questions.q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the USA?
questions.fact: It was a gift in 1886 to celebrate friendship between the two countries.

questions.q: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.fact: The yen has been Japan's money since 1871.

questions.q: How many players does one football team have on the pitch?
questions.fact: Including the goalkeeper.

questions.q: Which river flows through London?
questions.fact: The Thames is about 215 miles long.

questions.q: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.fact: It is smaller than most city parks, at around 44 hectares.

questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris and is one of the most famous paintings ever.

questions.q: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.fact: Everest stands about 8,849 metres high.

questions.q: Which of these is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.fact: Au comes from 'aurum', the Latin word for gold.

questions.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.fact: The extra day is 29 February.

questions.q: Which city hosts the famous Running of the Bulls?
questions.fact: It is part of the San Fermín festival every July.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.fact: Guacamole comes from Mexico and its name comes from an Aztec word for avocado sauce.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air?
questions.fact: They use it, with sunlight and water, to make their food.

questions.q: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.fact: It hit an iceberg on its first voyage, in April 1912.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder stood in Alexandria?
questions.fact: The Pharos may have been over 100 metres tall.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.fact: Ottawa was chosen in 1857 partly because it sat between English and French Canada.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.fact: They are tuned to G, D, A and E.

questions.q: Which US state is nicknamed the Sunshine State?
questions.fact: Florida gets around 230 sunny days a year.

questions.q: What colour do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
questions.fact: Blue and yellow are primary colours, and green is the one they make together.

questions.q: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
questions.fact: A shuttlecock can fly off a racket at over 300 mph in top-level play.

questions.q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived?
questions.fact: It can grow to around 30 metres long.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.fact: Honeycomb cells are hexagons because they pack together with no gaps.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Spain?
questions.fact: Madrid is one of the highest capital cities in Europe.

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze, in degrees Celsius?
questions.fact: 32 is the freezing point in Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Which country is home to the city of Marrakech?
questions.fact: Marrakech is famous for its huge market square, Jemaa el-Fnaa.

questions.q: Which sea creature has three hearts?
questions.fact: Two pump blood to the gills and one to the rest of the body.

questions.q: What is the name of the long, thin strip of land that links North and South America?
questions.fact: The Panama Canal was cut through it, opening in 1914.
